messages.author: 17c3b773431b7afe
messages.subject: combining hxsurf files
parts:
Hi Greg, 

I've had great success with the code below, in so far as getting data in and being able to use it, plot it, etc. However, there are some plots I want to make for which the data structure built below makes clunky. If possible, I'd like to make one large list of all my surfaces, instead of a list of surface lists, if that makes sense. 

This code goes through the folder with all my label field files, and imports the data into a list:

for (i in 1:length(list_surf_filenames)) # Reads folder data, puts it in appropriate num of files
  {
    n <- n+1
    df_surf[[n]]<-list_surf_filepath %>%           # full file path without file name
      file.path(list_surf_filenames[[i]]) %>%        # open this file from the above path
      read.hxsurf()                                  # reads amira binary hx surface file
  }

I thought maybe nat::union(df1,df2) would do the trick, but I just git another list of lists. Any ideas, or is this just the nature of the data structure?

BTW, thanks so much for making all this possible! I'd be up a creek without a paddle without the nat package. 

Thanks, 
Andy

messages.author: 7f0257cd1389289f
messages.subject: Re: [nat-user] combining hxsurf files
parts:
Hi Andy, 

glad nat is proving useful. 

the c.hxsurf method of the c function should do what you want. 

Assuming you have read all the surfaces into a list called surfs, then you should be able to combine them all in one go like so:

megasurf = do.call(c, surfs) 

You need a recent install of the GitHub version of nat. 

There is actually another route making use of neuronlist objects to make a list of surfaces behave like a single object (even if they remain separate)

surfnl = as.neuronlist(surfs)
plot3d(surfnl)

Should also work. 

Best,

Greg. 

Sent from my iPhone
